<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Principal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"Service"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"lambda.amazonaws.com"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"sts:AssumeRole"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The permission policy is the one from "Identity or resource", attached to <code>Reader</code> and allowing reads of <code>reports</code>. When the Lambda reads a file, AWS checks the two in order:</p>
<ol>
<li>The Lambda asks to assume <code>Reader</code>.</li>
<li>AWS checks the trust policy: <code>lambda.amazonaws.com</code> is in <code>Principal</code>, so this is allowed.</li>
<li>The Lambda gets <code>Reader</code>'s temporary credentials.</li>
<li>The Lambda calls <code>s3:GetObject</code> with them.</li>
<li>AWS checks the permission policy: <code>reports/*</code> is allowed, so this is allowed.</li>
</ol>
<p>The trust policy needs a <code>Principal</code> and the permission policy doesn't, for the same reason as the bucket policy. A trust policy has no <code>Resource</code>, because the resource is the role itself. <code>validate-policy</code> rejects a trust policy that includes one with <code>ROLE_TRUST_POLICY_SYNTAX_ERROR_RESOURCE</code>.</p>
<p>How trust policies work is covered in <a href="/v2/iam-assume-role-trust-policy">assumeRole and trust policy</a>.</p>
<h2>Grant or cap</h2>
<p>Every policy so far grants access. A few others use the same shape but only set a ceiling and grant nothing themselves.</p>
<h3>Permissions boundary</h3>
<p>A permissions boundary attaches to an IAM user or role and has no <code>Principal</code>. Say <code>Reader</code>'s identity-based policy allows every S3 action:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Allow"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>Reader</code> also has a permissions boundary, <code>s3-read-only</code>, that allows only <code>s3:GetObject</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Allow"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:GetObject"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Both are the same kind of JSON, attached with different commands:</p>
<ul>
<li>Attached with <code>put-role-policy</code>, it's an identity-based policy. Several of them combine with <code>||</code>: one allow is enough.</li>
<li>Attached with <code>put-role-permissions-boundary</code> below, it's a permissions boundary, and it combines with the identity-based policy by <code>&#x26;&#x26;</code>, which the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html">IAM evaluation page</a> calls an intersection.</li>
</ul>
<p>So <code>Reader</code> can do only <code>s3:GetObject</code>, which both allow; an <code>s3:PutObject</code> call is denied.</p>
<p>A boundary has to exist as a managed policy first, then gets attached by its ARN:</p>
<pre><code>aws iam create-policy \
  --policy-name s3-read-only \
  --policy-document file://s3-read-only.json

aws iam put-role-permissions-boundary \
  --role-name Reader \
  --permissions-boundary arn:aws:iam::111122223333:policy/s3-read-only
</code></pre>
<h3>Session policy</h3>
<p>A session policy also only caps. Say the IAM user <code>ops</code> wants <code>Reader</code>'s permissions, but only to read <code>reports/q3.pdf</code> this time. They write that limit as <code>only-q3.json</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Allow"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:GetObject"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"arn:aws:s3:::reports/q3.pdf"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Then they assume <code>Reader</code> with this command, passing <code>only-q3.json</code> with <code>--policy</code>:</p>
<pre><code>aws sts assume-role \
  --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/Reader \
  --role-session-name read-q3 \
  --policy file://only-q3.json
</code></pre>
<p>AWS checks <code>Reader</code>'s trust policy first. The trust policy above lists only <code>lambda.amazonaws.com</code> as <code>Principal</code>, so for <code>ops</code> to assume the role, the trust policy needs another statement with <code>arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/ops</code> as <code>Principal</code>.</p>
<p>Once that passes, AWS gives <code>ops</code> temporary credentials whose permissions are <code>permission policy &#x26;&#x26; session policy</code>. The permission policy allows all of <code>reports/*</code>, <code>only-q3.json</code> only <code>reports/q3.pdf</code>, so they can read only <code>q3.pdf</code>. Even if <code>only-q3.json</code> were <code>s3:*</code>, a call to <code>s3:PutObject</code> would still be denied, because the permission policy allows only <code>s3:GetObject</code>. The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html">IAM policy types page</a> says permissions boundaries and session policies both "do not grant permissions."</p>
<p>Trust policies and session policies both show up when a role is assumed, but they're stored and set at different times:</p>






























<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Trust policy</th><th>Session policy</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Stored where</td><td>On the <code>Reader</code> role</td><td>Not saved by AWS; it lives only with this session</td></tr><tr><td>Set how</td><td><code>create-role --assume-role-policy-document</code>, later <code>update-assume-role-policy</code></td><td><code>--policy</code> on each <code>assume-role</code> call</td></tr><tr><td>Checked when</td><td>Every time someone assumes <code>Reader</code></td><td>On every request made with these temporary credentials, until they expire (1 hour by default)</td></tr><tr><td>Decides</td><td>Who may assume <code>Reader</code></td><td>What these credentials may do at most after the assume</td></tr></tbody></table>
<h3>SCP</h3>
<p>An SCP (service control policy) limits every IAM user and role below where it's attached. An organization looks roughly like this:</p>
<pre><code>organization root
├── management account   ← created the organization, pays the whole organization's bill
├── OU: prod
│   ├── account A
│   └── account B
└── OU: dev
    └── account C
</code></pre>
<p>Say this SCP is attached to the organization root:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Deny"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:DeleteBucket"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<ul>
<li>A user in account A, B or C who calls <code>s3:DeleteBucket</code> is denied, even if their identity-based policy allows <code>s3:*</code>.</li>
<li>Users and roles in the management account aren't affected when they call <code>s3:DeleteBucket</code>. The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html">SCP page</a> says SCPs don't affect users or roles in the management account, or service-linked roles.</li>
</ul>
<p>Attach the same SCP to <code>OU: prod</code> instead, and only accounts A and B are limited.</p>
<p>Because SCPs can't limit the management account, the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_best-practices_mgmt-acct.html">Organizations best practices for the management account</a> recommend keeping resources in other accounts.</p>
<h3>RCP</h3>
<p>An <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/introducing-resource-control-policies-rcps-a-new-authorization-policy/">RCP</a> (Resource Control Policy), added in November 2024, attaches to the account that owns the bucket and also limits accounts outside the organization. This one, from the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_rcps_syntax.html">RCP syntax page</a>, denies any S3 request not made over HTTPS:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Deny"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Principal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Condition"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"BoolIfExists"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"aws:SecureTransport"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"false"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> } }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>An RCP you write can only use <code>Deny</code>; <code>Allow</code> appears only in <code>RCPFullAWSAccess</code>, which AWS attaches automatically and which lets every request through. Like SCPs, RCPs don't affect resources in the management account (see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_rcps.html">RCP page</a>).</p>
<h3>VPC endpoint policy</h3>
<p>An S3 <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html">gateway endpoint</a> lets EC2 instances in a VPC reach S3 without an internet gateway or NAT. The VPC endpoint policy on it limits what requests through it can reach. If the endpoint is created without a policy, AWS attaches a default one that allows everything. The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-access.html">VPC endpoint policy page</a> says an endpoint policy must have a <code>Principal</code>, and for a gateway endpoint it can only be <code>*</code>. Say the endpoint policy on an S3 gateway endpoint is this:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Allow"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Principal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:GetObject"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"arn:aws:s3:::reports/*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Code in the VPC going through that endpoint can read only <code>reports</code>. The endpoint policy only caps; whether <code>Reader</code> can read <code>reports</code> still comes down to its identity-based policy and the bucket policy.</p>
<h2>What about "deny everyone except X"?</h2>
<p><code>Principal</code> has a negated form, <code>NotPrincipal</code>. This bucket policy denies everyone except <code>Admin</code> access to <code>reports</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Deny"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "NotPrincipal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"AWS"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">    "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">    "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/Admin"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ]},</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"arn:aws:s3:::reports"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"arn:aws:s3:::reports/*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_notprincipal.html">IAM NotPrincipal page</a> allows <code>NotPrincipal</code> only with <code>Deny</code>, and never in an identity-based policy or a trust policy. It also recommends against <code>NotPrincipal</code> in new policies, in favour of <code>"Principal": "*"</code> with an <code>ArnNotEquals</code> condition on <code>aws:PrincipalArn</code>.</p>
<h2>Which policies have rules of their own?</h2>
<p><span id="kms"></span></p>
<h3>KMS key policy</h3>
<p>Usually, if <code>Reader</code>'s identity-based policy allows <code>s3:GetObject</code> and <code>kms:Decrypt</code>, it can read KMS-encrypted files (see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html">S3 SSE-KMS page</a>).</p>
<p>That's because the default key policy has a statement whose <code>Principal</code> is the account itself (<code>:root</code>). Once the key policy allows the account, KMS looks at the account's identity-based policies (see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-default.html">KMS default key policy page</a>). If a hand-written key policy leaves this statement out, <code>Reader</code> is denied even with <code>kms:Decrypt</code> in its identity-based policy.</p>
<p>The <code>+</code> lines below are that statement:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">   "Statement": [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">     {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">       "Sid": "Allow access for Key Administrators",</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">       ...</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">     },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+    {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+      "Sid": "Enable IAM User Permissions",</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+      "Effect": "Allow",</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:root" },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+      "Action": "kms:*",</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+      "Resource": "*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+    }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">   ]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<pre><code>S3:  identity policy || bucket policy || ACL
KMS: key policy names Reader || (key policy names :root &#x26;&#x26; identity policy)
</code></pre>
<h3>CloudFormation stack policy</h3>
<p>A CloudFormation stack policy controls which resources a stack update may change. This one allows every update except deletes (example from the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/protect-stack-resources.html">CloudFormation stack policy page</a>):</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Allow"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "NotAction"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Update:Delete"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Principal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>Principal</code> is required but accepts only <code>*</code>, since there is no "who" to pick. The actions aren't a service's API either; there are three, <code>Update:Modify</code>, <code>Update:Replace</code> and <code>Update:Delete</code>.</p>
<p><span id="check"></span></p>
<h2>What does <code>Reader</code> need to read <code>reports/q3.pdf</code>?</h2>
<p>For <code>Reader</code> reading <code>q3.pdf</code> in the same account, the rules on the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic_policy-eval-denyallow.html">IAM policy evaluation page</a> come out as a boolean expression, where any layer that isn't attached counts as <code>true</code>:</p>
<pre><code>no Deny matches
&#x26;&#x26; (identity policy 1 || identity policy 2 || bucket policy || ACL)
&#x26;&#x26; permissions boundary
&#x26;&#x26; session policy
&#x26;&#x26; SCP &#x26;&#x26; RCP &#x26;&#x26; VPC endpoint policy
&#x26;&#x26; kms:Decrypt   (if q3.pdf is encrypted with a KMS key)
</code></pre>
<p>Every <code>Deny</code> counts on the first line, whether it sits in the bucket policy, an identity policy or an SCP. The other lines look only at whether that policy has an <code>Allow</code>: the <code>bucket policy</code> in the parentheses, for example, asks whether the bucket policy has an <code>Allow</code> statement that permits this request.</p>
<p>The bucket policy in "Identity or resource" names <code>Reader</code>'s role ARN (<code>role/Reader</code>) as <code>Principal</code>. <code>Principal</code> can also name an IAM user's ARN, or the ARN of one session after the assume (<code>assumed-role/Reader/&#x3C;session name></code>). A November 2026 test tried all three. An IAM user and a role were created in the test bucket's account with no identity policy attached, so only the bucket policy could let them read. The role ARN and the session ARN were each tested twice, once with a permissions boundary and once with a session policy. The IAM user calls with an access key and has no session, so it was tested with the boundary only. Both the boundary and the session policy allow only <code>s3:ListBucket</code>, not <code>s3:GetObject</code>, so by the expression above every case should be denied:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>bucket policy <code>Principal</code></th><th>with a permissions boundary</th><th>with a session policy</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>IAM user ARN (<code>user/...</code>)</td><td>reads</td><td>n/a, a user calling directly has no session</td></tr><tr><td>role ARN (<code>role/Reader</code>)</td><td>denied</td><td>denied</td></tr><tr><td>role session ARN (<code>assumed-role/Reader/&#x3C;session name></code>)</td><td>reads</td><td>reads</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>In the first and third rows the expression predicts a denial, but the read succeeds. When the bucket policy names an IAM user or role session ARN, the boundary and session policy only limit what identity policies grant, and lines two to four of the expression become:</p>
<pre><code>&#x26;&#x26; ((identity policy 1 || identity policy 2) &#x26;&#x26; permissions boundary &#x26;&#x26; session policy
    || bucket policy || ACL)
</code></pre>
<p>The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html">IAM permissions boundaries page</a> lists the same three cases but doesn't say why a role ARN and a session ARN behave differently.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html">IAM policy types page</a> says "ACLs cannot grant permissions to entities within the same account". An ACL grant can go to a group (such as <code>AllUsers</code> or <code>AuthenticatedUsers</code>) or directly to an account, and the sentence doesn't say which it means. A November 2026 test tried the two group grants. The test IAM user was in the bucket's account with no policies attached; its <code>ListObjectsV2</code> call was denied, so it had no other permission to use. It made signed reads of two objects, one whose ACL had only <code>AllUsers: READ</code> and one with only <code>AuthenticatedUsers: READ</code>, and got the content of both. So group grants count for same-account identities too, and the <code>ACL</code> term belongs in the parentheses. If the IAM sentence holds, it may mean grants made directly to an account; that kind wasn't tested.</p>
<p>Across accounts, the expression changes. Say <code>Reader</code> is in account A and <code>reports</code> in account B:</p>
<pre><code>same account:   identity policy 1 || identity policy 2 || bucket policy || ACL
cross-account:  (identity policy 1 || identity policy 2) &#x26;&#x26; (bucket policy || ACL)
</code></pre>
<p>Account A has to let <code>Reader</code> out, and account B has to let it in (see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic-cross-account.html">IAM cross-account evaluation page</a>).</p>
<h3>With ACLs on, an Allow-only bucket policy is undone however precise it is</h3>
<p>Say the bucket policy on <code>reports</code> lets in only <code>Reader</code>, and ACLs are still enabled. Someone uploads <code>q3.pdf</code> with <code>--acl public-read</code>:</p>
<pre><code>aws s3 cp q3.pdf s3://reports/ --acl public-read
</code></pre>
<ol>
<li><code>q3.pdf</code>'s ACL gains a grant: <code>AllUsers</code> may <code>READ</code>.</li>
<li>The bucket policy still names only <code>Reader</code>.</li>
<li>Anyone can GET the file's URL, unsigned, and read it.</li>
</ol>
<p>The grant looks like this. No <code>Effect</code>, no <code>Action</code>, no <code>Condition</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="xml" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="xml" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">&#x3C;</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Grant</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  &#x3C;</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Grantee</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1"> xsi:type</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">=</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Group"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    &#x3C;</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">URI</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">>http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AllUsers&#x3C;/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">URI</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  &#x3C;/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Grantee</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  &#x3C;</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Permission</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">>READ&#x3C;/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Permission</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">&#x3C;/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">Grant</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">></span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/acl-overview.html">S3 ACL page</a> says <code>AllUsers</code> means anyone, anonymous included. An anonymous request has no identity policy, so in the <a href="#check">expression for <code>Reader</code> reading <code>q3.pdf</code></a>, the second line comes down to <code>bucket policy || ACL</code>. The bucket policy doesn't name the anonymous request, but <code>ACL</code> is <code>true</code>, so that line holds and the anonymous request can read. To stop it, add the <code>Deny</code> below to the bucket policy. The first line, "no Deny matches", then fails, the whole expression is <code>false</code>, and the anonymous request is denied. The <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_variables.html">IAM policy variables page</a> says an anonymous request's <code>aws:PrincipalType</code> is <code>Anonymous</code>, so this denies only anonymous requests and leaves <code>Reader</code> alone:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Effect"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Deny"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Principal"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Action"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"s3:GetObject"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Resource"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"arn:aws:s3:::reports/*"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">  "Condition"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"StringEquals"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"aws:PrincipalType"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Anonymous"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> } }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<h3>Block Public Access: do public ACLs and bucket policies count?</h3>
<p>Block Public Access is four switches, each on or off on its own (see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-control-block-public-access.html">S3 Block Public Access page</a>). All four deal only with <em>public</em> ACLs and bucket policies. The page says an ACL is public if it grants anything to <code>AllUsers</code> or <code>AuthenticatedUsers</code>. A November 2026 check with <code>get-bucket-policy-status</code> showed which bucket policies S3 counts as public. All of them allow <code>s3:GetObject</code> and differ only in <code>Principal</code> and <code>Condition</code>:</p>








































<table><thead><tr><th><code>Principal</code></th><th><code>Condition</code></th><th>IsPublic</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>"*"</code></td><td>none</td><td><code>True</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>"*"</code></td><td><code>"aws:SecureTransport": "true"</code></td><td><code>True</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>"*"</code></td><td><code>StringLike</code> <code>"aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-*"</code></td><td><code>True</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>"*"</code></td><td><code>StringEquals</code> <code>"aws:SourceVpc": "vpc-91237329"</code></td><td><code>False</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>"*"</code></td><td><code>StringEquals</code> <code>"aws:SourceAccount": "&#x3C;account ID>"</code></td><td><code>False</code></td></tr><tr><td>an account ARN</td><td>none</td><td><code>False</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>S3 treats a bucket policy as public by default and only calls it non-public when every <code>Allow</code> names a fixed party (no wildcard, no policy variable in the value). The party can be an ARN in <code>Principal</code>. With <code>Principal: "*"</code>, a condition key from the page's list (such as <code>aws:SourceAccount</code>, <code>aws:SourceVpc</code> or <code>aws:SourceIp</code>) has to name it in <code>Condition</code>. <code>vpc-*</code> has a wildcard, so that policy is still public. <code>aws:SecureTransport</code> isn't on the list, so that one is public too. In the console's wording, two act on <em>new</em> ones and two on <em>any</em>:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>BlockPublicAcls</code>, <code>BlockPublicPolicy</code> (<em>new</em>): S3 rejects any attempt to write a public ACL or bucket policy. Existing ones are untouched.</li>
<li><code>IgnorePublicAcls</code>, <code>RestrictPublicBuckets</code> (<em>any</em>): existing ones aren't deleted, but stop working for outsiders. A public ACL doesn't count; a public bucket policy stops working for other accounts and anonymous requests, while same-account principals and AWS services can still use it (test below the same-account Reader table).</li>
</ul>
<p>The account and the organization can set these switches too. An access point can as well, but its settings affect only requests through that access point. A switch on at any level counts as on: if the account has <code>IgnorePublicAcls</code> on, public ACLs in <code>reports</code> don't count even though the bucket has it off. At the organization level all four go on or off together.</p>
<p>The embed below runs top to bottom in the order S3 checks a request. Pick who is asking, flip the settings, and the result shows at the top.</p>
<iframe src="/embeds/s3-access-tree" width="100%" height="794" style="border:0;display:block;margin:1.5rem 0 2.5rem" loading="lazy" title="S3 bucket settings tree: what decides whether q3.pdf can be read"></iframe>
<p>Two roles in the embed don't read. With <code>BlockPublicAcls</code> on, the uploader's <code>--acl public-read</code> upload gets 403 <code>AccessDenied</code>. With <code>BlockPublicPolicy</code> on, the admin writing a <code>Principal: "*"</code> bucket policy also gets 403 <code>AccessDenied</code>. Three kinds of caller read: anonymous, a same-account Reader and an other-account Reader, one table each below. The assumptions match the embed: account-level Block Public Access is off, no SCP gets in the way, and the KMS key policy has only the default <code>:root</code> statement (see <a href="#kms">KMS key policy</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Anonymous, reading <code>q3.pdf</code></strong></p>





















<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Condition</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>At least one of two paths</td><td>ACL: ACLs on, the <code>AllUsers</code> grant exists, <code>IgnorePublicAcls</code> off<br>policy: an Allow for <code>Principal: "*"</code>, <code>RestrictPublicBuckets</code> off</td></tr><tr><td>and</td><td>no Deny matches the anonymous request</td></tr><tr><td>and</td><td>SSE-S3. With SSE-KMS, an anonymous request has no identity and can't get <code>kms:Decrypt</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong>Same-account Reader, reading <code>q3.pdf</code></strong></p>

















<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Condition</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>At least one of these four holds</td><td>the IAM policy's Allow<br>the bucket policy's statement for Reader<br>the public statement<br>the ACL path (ACLs on, the grant exists, <code>IgnorePublicAcls</code> off)</td></tr><tr><td>and</td><td>SSE-S3; or SSE-KMS with <code>:root</code> in the key policy and <code>kms:Decrypt</code> in the IAM policy</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Same-account requests aren't affected by <code>RestrictPublicBuckets</code>. The page says that with it on, S3 still allows "authorized users within the bucket owner's account", but doesn't define authorized. In the November 2026 test, <code>RestrictPublicBuckets</code> was on and the bucket policy had only a <code>Principal: "*"</code> Allow; a same-account IAM user with no policies read the object's content, while an anonymous request got 403. So even with no IAM permissions, a same-account IAM user counts as authorized.</p>
<p><strong>Other-account Reader, reading <code>q3.pdf</code></strong></p>

























<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Condition</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Reader's own account</td><td>the IAM policy has an Allow</td></tr><tr><td>and at least one on the <code>reports</code> side</td><td>the statement for Reader<br>the public statement<br>the ACL path</td></tr><tr><td>and not</td><td>a public bucket policy with <code>RestrictPublicBuckets</code> on, which blocks cross-account access entirely</td></tr><tr><td>and</td><td>SSE-S3. The key policy's <code>:root</code> is the account that owns <code>reports</code>, so an other-account Reader can't get <code>kms:Decrypt</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<h3>The 2023 defaults</h3>
<p><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/heads-up-amazon-s3-security-changes-are-coming-in-april-of-2023/">Since April 2023</a>, new buckets have all four on and <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/about-object-ownership.html">ACLs disabled</a> ("Bucket owner enforced"). With ACLs disabled:</p>
<ul>
<li>the <code>--acl public-read</code> upload above fails with a 400 <code>AccessControlListNotSupported</code>;</li>
<li>existing ACLs no longer take part in access evaluation; the <code>ACL</code> term in the expression is never true, and only the policies decide.</li>
</ul>
<h2>The takeaway</h2>
<p>Next time AWS hands you a new "X policy," ask two questions:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Does it name a who, with <code>Principal</code> or <code>NotPrincipal</code>?</strong> If yes, it sits on a resource; if no, on an identity. SCP and RCP are the exception.</li>
<li><strong>Does it grant access, or only cap it?</strong> If the docs say it does "not grant permissions," it only caps.</li>
</ol>
